title: Blaze template types, errors, discovery, and parsing (prd011 R1-R5, R9)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd011-blazes-templates.yaml (full PRD -- schema, discovery, listing, parsing, errors)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (package structure per Decisions 12 and 13)
  - docs/specs/use-cases/rel99.0-uc001-blazes-templates.yaml (use case success criteria S1-S3)
  - pkg/schema/ (existing struct definition patterns -- directory may be pkg/types/ in actual code; check go.mod module path and existing source)
  - pkg/api/ (existing sentinel error patterns -- directory may be pkg/types/ in actual code)
  - pkg/constants/ (existing domain string constants -- directory may be pkg/types/ in actual code)
  - go.mod (module path and existing YAML dependency for template parsing)

files:
  - path: pkg/schema/blaze.go
    action: create
    note: "BlazeTemplate, BlazeParameter, BlazeMetadata, TaskContext, SelectionResult, ExtractedParameter structs"
  - path: pkg/api/blaze.go
    action: create
    note: "Sentinel errors for blaze operations (ErrTemplateDirNotFound, ErrTemplateDirNotReadable, ErrTemplateNotFound, ErrMalformedTemplate, ErrNoMatch)"
  - path: pkg/constants/blaze.go
    action: create
    note: "Parameter type constants (text, integer, boolean, list) and default blazes directory path"
  - path: internal/blazes/discovery.go
    action: create
    note: "DiscoverTemplateDir and ListTemplates functions"
  - path: internal/blazes/parser.go
    action: create
    note: "ParseTemplates function with template and parameter schema validation"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Define BlazeTemplate struct with required fields (name string, description string, tags []string) and optional fields (parameters []BlazeParameter, trail_definition any, version string, priority int, author string) per prd011 R1.2-R1.11. All fields must have YAML struct tags matching the lowercase field names from prd011 R1.3 and R1.11. Optional fields use omitempty."
  - id: R2
    text: "Define BlazeParameter struct with fields name (string), description (string), type (string), and default (any) per prd011 R2.1-R2.9. Include YAML struct tags. The type field accepts exactly four values: text, integer, boolean, list per prd011 R2.5-R2.6."
  - id: R3
    text: "Define supporting structs used by later blazes features: BlazeMetadata per prd011 R5.7 with 8 fields (Name, Description, Tags, Parameters, Version, Priority, Author, FilePath), TaskContext per prd011 R6.2 with 3 fields (Description, Labels, Keywords), SelectionResult per prd011 R7.7 with 4 fields (Selected *BlazeMetadata, Tied []BlazeMetadata, Ambiguous bool, NoMatch bool), ExtractedParameter per prd011 R8.7 with 7 fields (Name, Description, Type, Default, Required, InferredValue, Inferred)."
  - id: R4
    text: "Define five sentinel errors per prd011 R9.1-R9.9: ErrTemplateDirNotFound (directory does not exist), ErrTemplateDirNotReadable (permissions prevent reading), ErrTemplateNotFound (specific template by name not found), ErrMalformedTemplate (valid YAML but violates schema), ErrNoMatch (no templates matched task context). All must be checkable with errors.Is. Use base sentinel with fmt.Errorf wrapping to include contextual information (path, underlying OS error) per R9.4-R9.5."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement DiscoverTemplateDir(explicitPath string, configBlazesDir string, dataDir string) (string, error) per prd011 R3.1-R3.6. Precedence: (1) explicitPath if non-empty, (2) configBlazesDir if non-empty, (3) well-known path .crumbs/blazes/ relative to dataDir. Verify directory exists with os.Stat -- return ErrTemplateDirNotFound wrapping the attempted path if not found, ErrTemplateDirNotReadable wrapping path and OS error if permission denied. Discovery is read-only and must not create directories or modify the filesystem per R3.6."
  - id: R6
    text: "Implement ListTemplates(templateDir string) ([]string, error) per prd011 R4.1-R4.6. Read directory entries with os.ReadDir. Include files with .yaml or .yml extension (case-insensitive check). Skip subdirectories and non-regular files per R4.5. Do not recurse into subdirectories per R4.3. Return absolute file paths sorted alphabetically by filename per R4.6. Return empty slice without error for empty directories per R4.4."
  - id: R7
    text: "Implement ParseTemplates(filePaths []string) ([]BlazeMetadata, []string) per prd011 R5.1-R5.8. The second return value is a list of warning messages for skipped files. For each file: read contents, parse YAML into BlazeTemplate struct, validate schema (non-empty name per R1.4, non-empty description per R1.5, non-empty tags list per R1.6, each tag lowercase letters/numbers/hyphens per R1.7, parameter names non-empty and valid format per R2.3, parameter descriptions non-empty per R2.4, parameter types recognized per R2.5, parameter names unique within template per R2.8, default value matches parameter type per R2.9). Convert valid templates to BlazeMetadata with FilePath set to the source file. Skip files with invalid YAML syntax or schema violations -- record a warning with filename and error per R5.3-R5.4 -- and continue processing remaining files. Unknown YAML fields are silently ignored per R1.10/R5.8."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Place struct definitions in the package where existing entity structs live. The ARCHITECTURE document says pkg/schema/ (Decision 12), but PRDs reference pkg/types/. Check the actual codebase and follow the existing pattern. Name the file blaze.go in that package."
  - id: D2
    text: "Place sentinel errors in the package where existing Cupboard and Table errors are defined. Follow the pattern from prd001-cupboard-core R7. Define base sentinels with errors.New; implementation code wraps them with fmt.Errorf and %w to add context (path, OS error) while remaining checkable with errors.Is."
  - id: D3
    text: "Place parameter type constants (BlazeParamTypeText, BlazeParamTypeInteger, BlazeParamTypeBoolean, BlazeParamTypeList) and default directory constant (BlazeDefaultDir = \".crumbs/blazes\") in the constants package per ARCHITECTURE Decision 13. No magic string literals in implementation code."
  - id: D4
    text: "Discovery, listing, and parsing are standalone functions in internal/blazes/, not part of the Table interface, per prd011 non-goals. Functions accept explicit parameters (paths, config values) rather than requiring a Cupboard reference, keeping them testable in isolation."
  - id: D5
    text: "Use the YAML library already in go.mod (gopkg.in/yaml.v3 from cobra/viper dependency chain). Parse with yaml.Unmarshal into BlazeTemplate struct. The default yaml.Unmarshal behavior silently ignores unknown fields, satisfying prd011 R1.10 without additional configuration."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "BlazeTemplate struct compiles with fields Name, Description, Tags, Parameters, TrailDefinition, Version, Priority, Author and correct yaml struct tags."
  - id: AC2
    text: "BlazeParameter struct compiles with fields Name, Description, Type, Default and correct yaml struct tags."
  - id: AC3
    text: "BlazeMetadata, TaskContext, SelectionResult, and ExtractedParameter structs compile with all fields listed in prd011 R5.7, R6.2, R7.7, R8.7 respectively."
  - id: AC4
    text: "Five sentinel errors (ErrTemplateDirNotFound, ErrTemplateDirNotReadable, ErrTemplateNotFound, ErrMalformedTemplate, ErrNoMatch) are defined and checkable with errors.Is."
  - id: AC5
    text: "DiscoverTemplateDir selects the correct directory following the three-level precedence chain: explicit path takes priority over config value, which takes priority over well-known path relative to dataDir."
  - id: AC6
    text: "DiscoverTemplateDir returns ErrTemplateDirNotFound (wrapping path) for missing directories and ErrTemplateDirNotReadable (wrapping path and OS error) for permission-denied directories."
  - id: AC7
    text: "ListTemplates returns .yaml and .yml files (case-insensitive) sorted alphabetically by filename, skips subdirectories and non-regular files, and returns an empty slice for empty directories."
  - id: AC8
    text: "ParseTemplates produces BlazeMetadata for each valid template, skips malformed templates collecting warning strings, and ignores unknown YAML fields. Validation rejects: empty name, empty description, empty tags, invalid tag format, unrecognized parameter type, duplicate parameter names, type-mismatched defaults."

title: GH-16: Stress test: validate requirement decomposition against stitch budget
description:
Use a make-work style analysis to validate whether current PRD requirements can be implemented within stitch's 15-minute budget. This is a pre-generation validation step before running GH-15.

## Problem

The recurring failure mode across generation runs is measure proposing tasks that exceed stitch's budget. The causes vary (subsystem bundling, infrastructure costs, rate limits) but the root issue is the same: we lack a way to validate that a set of requirements is implementable in a single stitch window before running the pipeline.

## Output

A report (eng06) containing:
- Table of proposed tasks per release with sizing estimates
- Flagged tasks with failure risk and reason
- Suggested PRD changes if requirements are too coarse for stitch
- Recommended task ordering within each release

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every PRD across rel01.0 through rel03.1 is analyzed
- Each proposed task has LOC estimate, subsystem count, and risk flag
- At least one concrete PRD or sizing recommendation is made if violations are found
- Results inform whether GH-15 generation run can proceed or needs spec changes first

GitHub: petar-djukic/crumbs#16

title: Analyze rel01.0 and rel01.1 PRDs for stitch sizing
description:
## Required Reading
- docs/VISION.yaml
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml
- docs/road-map.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-cupboard-core.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd002-sqlite-backend.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd003-crumbs-interface.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd005-metadata-interface.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd009-cupboard-cli.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd010-configuration-directories.yaml
- docs/specs/use-cases/rel01.0-uc001-cupboard-lifecycle.yaml (and all rel01.0, rel01.1 use cases)
- docs/engineering/eng05-testing-strategy.yaml

## Files to Create
- docs/scratch/eng06-sizing-rel01.yaml (intermediate scratch; merged into eng06 later)

## Requirements

For every requirement group in each PRD relevant to rel01.0 and rel01.1, propose how stitch would decompose the implementation into tasks. Apply these sizing rules:
- Target 300-700 LOC production code per task
- Max 5 files per task
- Max 1 new subsystem boundary per task (e.g., pkg/api is one subsystem, internal/persistence/engine is another)
- Separate implementation tasks from test tasks

For each proposed task produce:
- Task name (verb phrase, e.g. "Implement Cupboard interface and Config")
- Release it belongs to (rel01.0 or rel01.1)
- PRD requirements covered (e.g., prd001 R1-R4)
- Estimated production LOC
- Estimated test LOC
- Subsystem boundaries crossed (count)
- Infrastructure dependencies (packages that must exist first in this release)
- Risk flag: LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH with reason

Flag HIGH when: LOC > 400 production, or subsystems > 1, or dependency not yet generated.

Write results to docs/scratch/eng06-sizing-rel01.yaml as a YAML list of task objects.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 6 PRDs covering rel01.0 and rel01.1 analyzed
- At least one proposed task per PRD requirement group
- Every task has: name, release, prds_covered, loc_prod, loc_test, subsystems, dependencies, risk, risk_reason
- docs/scratch/eng06-sizing-rel01.yaml exists and is valid YAML

Pay particular attention to cross-subsystem interactions in these releases:

For each proposed task produce the same fields as the previous sub-issue:

title: Write eng06: stitch budget validation report
description:
## Required Reading
- docs/scratch/eng06-sizing-rel01.yaml (from sub-issue 1)
- docs/scratch/eng06-sizing-rel02-03.yaml (from sub-issue 2)
- docs/engineering/eng02-generation-workflow.yaml (for generation context)
- docs/engineering/eng05-testing-strategy.yaml (for testing expectations per release)
- docs/constitutions/design.yaml (engineering-guideline format)

## Files to Create
- docs/engineering/eng06-stitch-budget-validation.yaml

## Files to Delete
- docs/scratch/eng06-sizing-rel01.yaml
- docs/scratch/eng06-sizing-rel02-03.yaml

## Requirements

Aggregate both sizing tables into a single engineering guideline following the engineering-guideline-format from docs/constitutions/design.yaml (required fields: id, title, introduction, sections).

The report must include:

1. A summary section: total proposed task count per release, total estimated LOC, and overall risk assessment (can GH-15 proceed as-is?)

2. A per-release section for each of rel01.0, rel01.1, rel02.0, rel02.1, rel03.0, rel03.1 containing:
   - A named table of proposed tasks with all sizing fields
   - Narrative on the highest-risk tasks and why they are risky

3. A recommendations section:
   - Flag any tasks where LOC > 400 production or subsystems > 1 and propose how to split them
   - Recommend task ordering within each release (which tasks must come before others)
   - If PRD requirements are too coarse, name the specific requirement group and suggest how to refine it

4. A go/no-go conclusion:
   - PROCEED: all releases have tasks within stitch budget with LOW/MEDIUM risk
   - PROCEED WITH CAUTION: some HIGH-risk tasks exist but workarounds are documented
   - HOLD: spec changes required before GH-15 can run

Delete the scratch files after writing eng06.

## Acceptance Criteria
- docs/engineering/eng06-stitch-budget-validation.yaml exists and passes mage analyze (no schema errors)
- All 6 releases covered with named sizing tables
- At least one concrete recommendation made (split, reorder, or refine a PRD)
- Go/no-go conclusion present with rationale
- Scratch files deleted
- mage analyze exits clean after changes

title: Fix prd002 R7 Error Handling: populate empty items list
description:

R7 in prd002-sqlite-backend.yaml has `items: []` — an empty list that fails mage analyze schema validation. Populate R7.items with concrete error handling requirements covering:

- R7.1: Corrupt or malformed JSONL lines (skip and warn behavior)
- R7.2: Missing or unreadable DataDir on Attach

title: Audit all YAML spec files for constitution formatting violations
description:
## Required Reading
- docs/constitutions/design.yaml (forbidden_terms, formatting, document_types, completeness_checklists)
- All files under docs/specs/product-requirements/ (12 PRDs)
- All files under docs/specs/use-cases/ (23 use cases)
- All files under docs/engineering/ (engineering guidelines)

## Files to Modify
- Any files found to violate constitution rules (expected: subset of the above)

## Requirements

Audit every YAML file in docs/specs/ and docs/engineering/ for:

1. Forbidden terms: critical, critically, key, deliberate, strategic, precisely, absolutely, fundamental, breakthrough, principled, honest, at the heart of, grounded, standards-aligned
2. Voice violations: passive voice or "This document describes..." instead of "We..."
3. Missing required fields per document type schema (PRD: id, title, problem, goals, requirements, non_goals, acceptance_criteria; use case: id, title, summary, actor, trigger, flow, touchpoints, success_criteria, out_of_scope)
4. Title/content conventions: engineering guidelines must have sections with both title and content fields; PRDs must have requirements with both title and items fields

Fix all violations found. Do not alter meaning or restructure content beyond what the constitution requires.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Zero forbidden terms in any audited file
- All PRDs have non-empty non_goals and acceptance_criteria
- All engineering guidelines have sections with title and content fields
- mage analyze reports zero constitution drift
